subproblem.title: A negatively oriented orthonormal frame σ of ν^⊥: det[ν, σ] = −1
subproblem.statement: Let n ≥ 1 and ν ∈ ℝ^{n+1} with |ν| = 1. For x ∈ ℝ^{n+1} and a family a = (a_0, …, a_{n−1}) in ℝ^{n+1}, let [x, a] be the (n+1)×(n+1) real matrix whose column 0 is x and whose column l+1 is a_l (its entry in row r, column c is the r-th coordinate of the c-th column vector). Then there is an orthonormal family σ = (σ_0, …, σ_{n−1}) in ℝ^{n+1} with span{σ_0, …, σ_{n−1}} = (span{ν})^⊥ and det[ν, σ] = −1.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (ν : Euclid (n + 1)), 1 ≤ n → ‖ν‖ = 1 → ∃ σ : Fin n → Euclid (n + 1), Orthonormal ℝ σ ∧ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range σ) = (Submodule.span ℝ {ν})ᗮ ∧ Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun r c : Fin (n + 1) => (Fin.cons ν σ : Fin (n + 1) → Euclid (n + 1)) c r) = -1
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 (Oriented frame) of the parent proof, with the sign normalization written uniformly.

Notation. ⟨·,·⟩ is the standard inner product of ℝ^{n+1} and x_r is the r-th coordinate of x ∈ ℝ^{n+1}. For x ∈ ℝ^{n+1} and a = (a_0, …, a_{n−1}), [x, a] is the matrix with entries [x, a]_{r,c} = (c-th vector of (x, a_0, …, a_{n−1}))_r; in Lean it is Matrix.of fun r c => (Fin.cons x a : Fin (n + 1) → Euclid (n + 1)) c r, so column 0 holds x and column l+1 (= Fin.succ l) holds a_l. Indices of σ and τ range over Fin n = {0, …, n−1}.

1. (Dimension.) Since |ν| = 1, ν ≠ 0, so span{ν} is 1-dimensional and Q := (span{ν})^⊥ has dimension (n+1) − 1 = n, because dim V + dim V^⊥ = dim ℝ^{n+1} = n+1 for every subspace V (Mathlib: Submodule.finrank_orthogonal_span_singleton, with finrank ℝ (Euclid (n+1)) = n+1 from finrank_euclideanSpace_fin).
2. (Orthonormal basis of Q.) Choose an orthonormal basis (q_0, …, q_{n−1}) of Q indexed by Fin n (for instance stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ Q reindexed along finCongr of the equality finrank Q = n from step 1), and let τ_k ∈ ℝ^{n+1} be q_k regarded as a vector of ℝ^{n+1}. The inner product of Q is the restriction of that of ℝ^{n+1}, so τ = (τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) is orthonormal in ℝ^{n+1} (Orthonormal.comp_linearIsometry with the inclusion Q.subtypeₗᵢ). The q_k span Q, so the τ_k span the image of Q under the inclusion, which is Q itself: span{τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}} = Q (Submodule.span_image, Submodule.map_top, Submodule.range_subtype).
3. (τ_k ⊥ ν.) Each τ_k lies in Q = (span{ν})^⊥, hence ⟨ν, τ_k⟩ = 0 (Submodule.mem_orthogonal_singleton_iff_inner_right).
4. (u := (ν, τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) is an orthonormal basis of ℝ^{n+1}.) Put u_0 := ν and u_{l+1} := τ_l, i.e. u = Fin.cons ν τ. Then ⟨u_0, u_0⟩ = |ν|² = 1; ⟨u_0, u_{l+1}⟩ = ⟨u_{l+1}, u_0⟩ = ⟨ν, τ_l⟩ = 0 by step 3 and symmetry; and ⟨u_{l+1}, u_{m+1}⟩ = ⟨τ_l, τ_m⟩ = δ_{lm} by step 2. So u is an orthonormal family of n+1 vectors (orthonormal_iff_ite, checked by cases on whether each index is 0 or a successor). It is linearly independent, and since its cardinality n+1 equals dim ℝ^{n+1}, it spans ℝ^{n+1} (LinearIndependent.span_eq_top_of_card_eq_finrank'); hence u is an orthonormal basis of ℝ^{n+1} (OrthonormalBasis.mk).
5. (d := det[ν, τ] satisfies d·d = 1.) Let W := [ν, τ], so W_{r,c} = (u_c)_r. For all c, c' we have (WᵀW)_{c,c'} = Σ_r (u_c)_r (u_{c'})_r = ⟨u_c, u_{c'}⟩ = δ_{cc'}, so WᵀW = I and d² = det(Wᵀ)·det(W) = det(WᵀW) = 1. (Equivalently: det W is the determinant of the orthonormal basis u with respect to the standard orthonormal basis EuclideanSpace.basisFun, by Module.Basis.det_apply, and that determinant is 1 or −1 by OrthonormalBasis.det_to_matrix_orthonormalBasis_real.) Hence d ∈ {1, −1} and d·d = 1.
6. (Sign normalization.) Since n ≥ 1, the index 0 ∈ Fin n exists. Define σ_0 := (−d)·τ_0 and σ_l := τ_l for l ≠ 0, i.e. σ := Function.update τ 0 ((−d)•τ_0). (If d = 1 this replaces τ_0 by −τ_0; if d = −1 it leaves τ unchanged — exactly the case distinction of the parent proof.)
7. (σ is orthonormal.) ⟨σ_0, σ_0⟩ = (−d)²⟨τ_0, τ_0⟩ = d·d = 1. For l ≠ 0: ⟨σ_0, σ_l⟩ = (−d)⟨τ_0, τ_l⟩ = 0 and ⟨σ_l, σ_0⟩ = (−d)⟨τ_l, τ_0⟩ = 0. For l, m ≠ 0: ⟨σ_l, σ_m⟩ = ⟨τ_l, τ_m⟩ = δ_{lm}. Hence ⟨σ_l, σ_m⟩ = δ_{lm} for all l, m, i.e. σ is orthonormal (orthonormal_iff_ite).
8. (span σ = (span{ν})^⊥.) Each σ_l is a scalar multiple of τ_l, so every σ_l lies in span{τ} and span{σ} ⊆ span{τ}. Conversely, τ_0 = (−d)·σ_0 because (−d)·(−d) = d·d = 1, and τ_l = σ_l for l ≠ 0, so every τ_l lies in span{σ} and span{τ} ⊆ span{σ}. Therefore span{σ} = span{τ} = Q = (span{ν})^⊥ by step 2.
9. (det[ν, σ] = −1.) The matrices [ν, σ] and W coincide except in column 1 = Fin.succ 0, which holds σ_0 = (−d)·τ_0 in [ν, σ] and τ_0 in W; indeed Fin.cons ν (Function.update τ 0 y) = Function.update (Fin.cons ν τ) (Fin.succ 0) y (Fin.cons_update). The determinant is linear in each column (Matrix.det_updateCol_smul; equivalently AlternatingMap.map_update_smul for the standard-basis determinant), so det[ν, σ] = (−d)·det W = −(d·d) = −1.
10. By steps 7, 8 and 9, σ is an orthonormal family in ℝ^{n+1} with span{σ_0, …, σ_{n−1}} = (span{ν})^⊥ and det[ν, σ] = −1. ∎
proof_key_steps: Q = (span{ν})^⊥ has dimension n; an orthonormal basis τ of Q (stdOrthonormalBasis reindexed to Fin n) is orthonormal in ℝ^{n+1}, spans Q, and satisfies ⟨ν, τ_k⟩ = 0.
(ν, τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) is an orthonormal basis of ℝ^{n+1}, so d := det[ν, τ] is the determinant of an orthogonal matrix and d·d = 1.
Replace τ_0 by (−d)·τ_0 (possible as n ≥ 1): orthonormality and the span are preserved, and linearity of det in column 1 gives det[ν, σ] = −d·d = −1.
